([[Rolling Meadows, Illinois]]) | college = [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 46 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | career_start = 2024 | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–present | team1 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team2 = →[[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | highlights = * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team (2024) }} '''Cameron Hannaford Christie''' (born July 24, 2005) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Christie and his brother [[Max Christie|Max]], grew up in [[Arlington Heights, Illinois]], and attended [[Rolling Meadows High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/cameron-christie-basketball-rolling-meadows/|title=Cameron Christie continues family legacy on hardwood in Rolling Meadows|first=Matt|last=Zahn|website=[[CBS Chicago]]|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He averaged 22 points, four rebounds, and three assists per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2023/01/02/minnesota-recruit-cameron-christie-continues-to-develop-rapidly-for-rolling-meadows-just-like-his-brother-max-did-i-had-to-show-people/|title= Minnesota recruit Cameron Christie continues to develop rapidly for Rolling Meadows. Just like his brother Max did. 'I had to show people'.|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=January 2, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} Christie was rated a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] over offers from [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/7/29/23283689/cam-christie-rolling-meadows-minnesota-basketball|title=Rolling Meadows senior Cam Christie commits to Minnesota|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=July 29, 2022|access-date=March 19, 2024}} ==College career== Christie began his freshman season as a key reserve at guard.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-mens-basketball-cam-christie-big-ten-freshman-ben-johnson/600341729/|title=Gophers' Cam Christie makes case as one of Big Ten's best freshmen|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=February 7, 2024|access-date=March 20, 2024}} He made his college debut in the second game of the season against [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA]] and scored 18 points in a 102–76 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-mens-basketball-cam-christie-kris-humphries-ben-johnson-best-freshman-debut-2003/600319961/|title=Gophers men's basketball freshman Cam Christie delivers big debuts|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=November 15, 2023|access-date=March 20, 2024}} Christie made his first career start against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] on December 6, 2023, and scored nine points with three rebounds in a 76–65 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-basketball-dawson-garcia-injury-huge-first-half-deficit-stop-nebraska/600325000/|title=Gophers rally past Nebraska; star Dawson Garcia leaves game with injured ankle|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=December 7, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2024}} He was named to the [[Big Ten Conference]] All-Freshman team at the end of the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-mens-basketball-dawson-garcia-cam-christie-all-big-ten-teams/600350464/|title=Gophers' Dawson Garcia, Cam Christie named to All-Big Ten teams|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=March 10, 2024|access-date=March 19, 2024}} Following the end of the season, Christie declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/minnesota/article/minnesota-basketball-cameron-christie-declares-for-nba-draft-while-maintaining-eligibility-230339134/ |title=Minnesota Basketball: Cameron Christie Declares for NBA Draft While Maintaining Eligibility }} ==Professional career== On June 27, 2024, Christie was selected with the 46th overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Tomer|last=Azarly|title=LA Clippers select Cam Christie with 46th overall pick in NBA Draft|url=https://clutchpoints.com/clippers-news-la-selects-cam-christie-with-46th-overall-pick-in-nba-draft|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} and on July 5, he signed with them.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Clippers Sign Cam Christie To Four-Year Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/clippers-to-sign-cam-christie-to-four-year-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} Throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] several times.{{cite web|title=2024-2025 San Diego Clippers Transaction
